summary: Meyer defended cosmic beginnings and fine-tuning as design evidence; Halper more successfully emphasized theorem limits, unknown probabilities, testability, and underdetermined divine intentions.

pro.text: These are things we know from experience come from minds.
pro.context: Meyer invoked familiar mind-produced information and fine-tuning as positive causal background for extending a design inference to cosmic conditions.

con.text: all the observational evidence only tells us that there was a hot density
con.context: Halper distinguished observations supporting a hot early universe from evidence establishing a singularity or an absolute temporal beginning.

con-alternatives-disjunctive-uncertainty.words: Competing early-universe accounts justify substantial uncertainty about whether the hot Big Bang represents the universe's absolute beginning.
con-alternatives-disjunctive-uncertainty.critique: Strongest feature: The explicitly qualified appeal to multiple early-universe possibilities directly supports underdetermination, preserves uncertainty, and avoids pretending that any particular alternative has already received decisive empirical confirmation. Principal limitation: Merely cataloguing materially different models does not independently establish comparable scientific viability, because mathematical consistency, evidential motivation, and observational accessibility can differ substantially across the proposed possibilities. Live burden: The argument must distinguish genuinely developed competitors from speculative placeholders and explain why their collective availability materially lowers confidence in an absolute beginning rather than merely displaying incomplete contemporary knowledge. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional motion-level relevance, coherent calibration, and responsible qualification, while retaining a meaningful evidential limitation concerning the comparatively compressed transition from model plurality to substantial cosmological uncertainty.

con-science-faith-probabilistic-conflict.words: Faith and science need not conflict inherently, yet scriptural commitments can increase rejection of scientific conclusions when apparent contradictions arise.
con-science-faith-probabilistic-conflict.critique: Strongest feature: The carefully probabilistic framing distinguishes inherent incompatibility from an increased behavioral tendency, expressly includes reconciliation, and therefore represents religious responses with considerable qualification and argumentative charity. Principal limitation: The response-options analysis and reported American survey remain insufficiently developed to establish frequencies across scriptural traditions, institutional settings, cultures, or differently formulated conflicts between scientific findings and faith. Live burden: The argument must connect its limited survey evidence to the broader causal generalization while separating scriptural commitment itself from education, community pressure, prior ideology, and disputed interpretations of what constitutes scientific fact. Locked score: The strong band recognizes logical clarity, relevant empirical support, and unusually fair scope control, while preserving the locked concern that the evidential bridge from a reported population sample to the generalized probabilistic claim remains compressed.

pro-epistemic-biblical-science.words: Biblical concepts of natural law, rational intelligibility, and contingent creation historically encouraged systematic empirical investigation of nature.
pro-epistemic-biblical-science.critique: Strongest feature: The historical thesis identifies three intelligible theological contributions to empirical inquiry and supplies relevant contrary context against any simplistic portrayal of scriptural belief as intrinsically hostile to science. Principal limitation: It leaves the extent, distinctiveness, and historical causal importance of those contributions insufficiently qualified, especially relative to other intellectual traditions, institutions, technologies, and ordinary motivations for systematic investigation. Live burden: More importantly, the reply must address whether scriptural commitment can increase rejection of scientific conclusions during apparent conflict, because historical encouragement of science does not resolve that specific probabilistic behavioral challenge. Locked score: The mixed band reflects a coherent and plausible subsidiary contribution with recognizable historical relevance, but also its partly unstable scope, limited comparative substantiation, and classification as a relevant nonanswer to the decisive preceding claim.

con-natural-motivation-for-science.words: Observable regularities, recurring astronomical patterns, and ordinary curiosity can motivate scientific inquiry without any necessary theological foundation.
con-natural-motivation-for-science.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly supplies an accessible alternative motivation for inquiry by grounding investigation in publicly observable regularities, recurring patterns, and ordinary curiosity rather than requiring antecedent theological commitments. Principal limitation: Demonstrating that natural observation is sufficient does not rebut the narrower historical proposition that biblical ideas contingently encouraged particular forms of modern systematic science, so the response partly targets an unnecessarily strong necessity reading. Live burden: The argument must compare explanatory contributions rather than merely establish logical independence, distinguishing universal curiosity from the institutional, conceptual, and methodological conditions associated with sustained scientific development. Locked score: The strong band reflects excellent direct contact, stable scope, matched calibration, and concrete illustrations, while retaining a representational limitation because the strongest source-supported version of the opposing historical claim remains only partially addressed.

pro-beginning-observation-theorems.words: Expansion, background radiation, galaxy ages, and major cosmological theorems cumulatively provide substantial, though nondeductive, evidence for a cosmic beginning.
pro-beginning-observation-theorems.critique: Strongest feature: The cumulative presentation integrates several observational considerations with named theoretical results and explicitly characterizes their combined force as substantial evidence rather than an exceptionless deductive demonstration. Principal limitation: The word beginning sometimes shifts between a hot early phase, a classical spacetime boundary, geodesic incompleteness, and absolute origination, although those conclusions require importantly different premises and theorem conditions. Live burden: The argument must specify what each observation or theorem independently establishes, identify its domain assumptions, and show how the resulting evidence supports an absolute cosmic beginning rather than merely an early boundary requiring further physics. Locked score: The very strong band recognizes high central relevance, coherent accumulation, substantial evidential warrant, and responsible qualification, while preserving the consequential scope ambiguity exposed by the boundary-versus-origin distinction.

pro-beginning-transcendent-cause.words: If matter, energy, space, and time began, their adequate cause must transcend them and possess volitional causal power.
pro-beginning-transcendent-cause.critique: Strongest feature: The conditional structure clearly connects the stipulated beginning of matter, energy, space, and time to an explanatory demand for a cause independent of ordinary material reality. Principal limitation: Excluding familiar material causes does not uniquely identify volitional agency, because unknown nonmaterial principles, boundary conditions, or fundamentally different explanatory categories remain conceptually available without being comparatively examined. Live burden: The argument must justify why transcendence and volition are necessary or especially probable attributes, explain causation without prior time, and demonstrate comparative adequacy rather than defining the proposed explanation through the desired conclusion. Locked score: The strong band reflects indispensable relevance to the central agency bridge and a recoverable conditional inference, while preserving the locked weaknesses in warrant, alternative consideration, representational charity, and the somewhat overstated claim of necessary causal adequacy.

con-hot-big-bang-not-singularity.words: Evidence for a hot, dense early universe does not itself establish a primordial singularity or an absolute beginning of time.
con-hot-big-bang-not-singularity.critique: Strongest feature: The reply draws the debate's decisive evidential distinction between observations supporting a hot dense early universe and the substantially stronger conclusion of a primordial singularity or absolute temporal beginning. Principal limitation: Its categorical wording about there being no empirical evidence risks understating how observations can indirectly support theoretical models whose backward extrapolations motivate boundary hypotheses, even when they do not directly observe a singularity. Live burden: The argument must preserve the difference between direct observation, model-mediated evidence, and theorem-dependent inference while explaining what confidence remains appropriate concerning an early boundary under incomplete quantum-gravity physics. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptionally direct diagnostic contact, stable terminology, central burden relevance, and strong logical discipline, with only a limited calibration concern about expressing the evidential denial too comprehensively.

con-classical-theorems-quantum-limit.words: Classical singularity theorems cannot establish an absolute beginning where quantum gravity supersedes their assumptions near extreme early-universe conditions.
con-classical-theorems-quantum-limit.critique: Strongest feature: The reply precisely identifies the domain limitation of classical singularity reasoning by emphasizing that extreme early-universe conditions require quantum-gravitational treatment beyond the established applicability of classical spacetime assumptions. Principal limitation: Showing that a theorem cannot govern the quantum regime does not positively establish extension beyond the boundary, and the absence of a completed quantum-gravity theory leaves the ultimate history genuinely unresolved. Live burden: The argument must explain which theorem assumptions fail, what candidate quantum frameworks replace them, and whether those replacements offer developed continuations rather than merely preserving logical possibilities against an absolute beginning. Locked score: The very strong band recognizes decisive diagnostic responsiveness, exceptionally high central relevance, calibrated uncertainty, and rigorous separation of theorem scope from metaphysical conclusion, while retaining the unavoidable limitation that the critique supports agnosticism rather than a contrary cosmological history.

pro-alternatives-quantum-inputs.words: Quantum-cosmological alternatives still presuppose mathematical structures, laws, boundary conditions, and information whose origins require explanation.
pro-alternatives-quantum-inputs.critique: Strongest feature: The reply correctly observes that invoking quantum cosmology does not eliminate every explanatory question, because formal structures, governing principles, states, boundary conditions, or informational specifications may remain presupposed. Principal limitation: An unexplained input is not automatically equivalent to the universe's unexplained origin, and the argument risks relocating distinct scientific and metaphysical explanatory standards into a single undifferentiated demand for ultimate explanation. Live burden: The case must identify which inputs are contingent, physically indispensable, and unusually specified, then demonstrate why a transcendent intelligent cause explains them better without introducing comparably substantial unexplained commitments. Locked score: The strong band reflects valuable burden contact, coherent scrutiny of naturalistic alternatives, and central comparative relevance, while preserving significant limitations concerning explanatory regress, category distinctions, and the insufficiently demonstrated transition from residual assumptions to intelligent causation.

pro-alternatives-bgv-costs.words: Inflationary or bouncing models subject to positive average expansion remain past-incomplete, while proposed escapes incur additional assumptions or fine-tuning.
pro-alternatives-bgv-costs.critique: Strongest feature: The reply engages alternative cosmologies on their own structural conditions by invoking average expansion, past incompleteness, and the additional theoretical commitments required by proposed evasions or bounce mechanisms. Principal limitation: Past incompleteness is not identical to absolute origination, and describing modifications as costs does not establish that they are ad hoc, empirically unsupported, or explanatorily inferior after independent motivations are considered. Live burden: The argument must separate theorem consequences from metaphysical conclusions and compare each alternative's total assumptions, predictive achievements, and fine-tuning liabilities against those of the proposed theistic explanation. Locked score: The very strong band reflects direct engagement, high central relevance, substantial technical coherence, and effective pressure on easy appeals to cosmological alternatives, while retaining material scope and comparative-accounting limitations that prevent the theorem from settling the ultimate beginning question.

con-models-require-tested-predictions.words: Early-universe proposals gain scientific standing through mathematical development and risky observational consequences, not merely by remaining logically possible.
con-models-require-tested-predictions.critique: Strongest feature: The methodological challenge appropriately distinguishes developed scientific models from bare possibilities by requiring mathematical articulation, observational consequences, and opportunities for empirical discrimination among competing early-universe accounts. Principal limitation: The standard can become excessively restrictive if applied as though direct near-origin testing were required, because historical sciences commonly use indirect evidence, explanatory integration, retrodiction, and comparative causal reasoning. Live burden: The argument must specify proportionate evidential thresholds for inaccessible regimes and apply them symmetrically to naturalistic cosmologies and design proposals, including each position's background assumptions and distinctive expectations. Locked score: The very strong band recognizes a powerful central criterion, direct contact with speculative alternatives, and disciplined emphasis on testability, while preserving the qualification that empirical evaluation admits more forms than novel precise prediction and must not exclude legitimate inference before decisive experiments become feasible.

pro-finetuning-narrow-ranges.words: Life depends on tightly constrained constants and initial conditions whose permissible ranges appear extraordinarily narrow relative to physically conceivable alternatives.
pro-finetuning-narrow-ranges.critique: Strongest feature: The constructive case identifies specific cosmological parameters and initial conditions as life-sensitive, thereby presenting fine-tuning as a concrete explanatory phenomenon rather than an impressionistic appeal to cosmic order. Principal limitation: Narrow life-permitting intervals do not by themselves establish improbability without a justified possibility space, parameter independence assumptions, probability measure, and treatment of alternative forms of complexity or observers. Live burden: The argument must show that the relevant quantities genuinely could vary, that the adopted ranges and measure are physically meaningful, and that selection effects or deeper mechanisms do not dissolve the claimed surprise. Locked score: The strong band reflects substantial central relevance, recognizable scientific motivation, and a coherent cumulative phenomenon, while preserving serious foundational limitations in probabilistic interpretation, range specification, and the transition from apparent sensitivity to comparative confirmation of intelligent design.

con-fine-tuning-measure-unknown.words: Without a justified possibility space and probability distribution for cosmic constants, narrow life-permitting ranges do not yield a reliable improbability claim.
con-fine-tuning-measure-unknown.critique: Strongest feature: The reply isolates the precise probabilistic foundation required by fine-tuning arguments: a defensible space of alternatives, an appropriate measure, and justified assumptions about how constants or conditions vary. Principal limitation: Failure to derive a unique probability distribution need not erase every form of comparative surprise, because robustness across plausible measures or mechanistic sensitivity could still provide nonnumerical evidential significance. Live burden: The argument must show whether reasonable candidate measures materially disagree, distinguish unknown probability from equal plausibility, and address fine-tuning claims framed through counterfactual sensitivity rather than exact numerical odds. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional diagnostic precision, direct central relevance, stable scope, and strong calibration, while preserving the narrower limitation that measure uncertainty constrains probabilistic confidence without automatically demonstrating that all fine-tuning evidence is explanatorily inert.

pro-finetuning-contingency-probability.words: Observed constants appear contingent rather than necessary, so their life-permitting combination remains probabilistically surprising and calls for comparative explanation.
pro-finetuning-contingency-probability.critique: Strongest feature: The reply properly focuses attention on contingency and resists treating currently unexplained constants as necessary merely because no deeper variation mechanism has yet been empirically established. Principal limitation: Apparent contingency does not supply a probability distribution, and moving from conceptual variability to probabilistic surprise risks treating ignorance about necessity or mechanism as affirmative evidence for low likelihood. Live burden: The argument must provide positive reasons for the relevant possibility space and measure, distinguish epistemic uncertainty from objective chance, and compare design with naturalistic selection mechanisms under symmetrical assumptions. Locked score: The strong band reflects direct engagement with the necessity response, meaningful relevance to the central fine-tuning bridge, and a plausible demand for explanation, while preserving the substantial evidential gap between lacking a known necessity theorem and possessing a warranted improbability estimate.

con-anthropic-constant-prediction.words: Anthropic multiverse reasoning generated a successful order-of-magnitude expectation for the cosmological constant, giving the framework some empirical credibility.
con-anthropic-constant-prediction.critique: Strongest feature: The reply offers a concrete predictive achievement rather than relying solely on multiverse possibility, connecting observer selection to an order-of-magnitude expectation for the subsequently measured cosmological constant. Principal limitation: One approximate success does not uniquely confirm the entire multiverse framework, because measure choices, selection assumptions, parameter correlations, and alternative explanations affect how strongly the observation discriminates among models. Live burden: The argument must reconstruct the prediction's timing, assumptions, tolerance, and comparative likelihood while showing that it was neither flexible accommodation nor a result obtainable under substantially different hypotheses. Locked score: The exceptional band reflects unusually strong evidential specificity, direct relevance to the demand for testable naturalistic consequences, and powerful comparative pressure on design, while preserving important questions about uniqueness, model dependence, and extrapolation from one parameter to a comprehensive cosmological explanation.

pro-comparative-design-multiverse.words: Fine-tuning is expected under theistic design, whereas multiverse explanation combines inflationary and landscape commitments and may therefore carry greater theoretical complexity.
pro-comparative-design-multiverse.critique: Strongest feature: The reply adopts an explicitly comparative framework, states an empirical expectation under design, and challenges whether a multiverse assembled from inflationary and landscape components actually improves total explanatory economy. Principal limitation: Counting theoretical components does not measure overall complexity, especially when those components possess independent motivation, while theism's agency, capacities, intentions, and selection principles also require inclusion in the comparison. Live burden: The argument must specify the design hypothesis sufficiently to generate discriminating likelihoods, answer the cited anthropic prediction, and compare total commitments and predictive performance under a common evidential standard. Locked score: The strong band reflects excellent motion-level relevance, coherent comparative structure, and meaningful scrutiny of multiverse costs, while preserving limited evidence, partly underspecified theistic expectations, and only partial contact with the strongest concrete naturalistic prediction.

pro-comparative-agency-causal-knowledge.words: Because minds produce functional information and finely adjusted systems, agency has positive causal relevance to analogous specificity in life and cosmology.
pro-comparative-agency-causal-knowledge.critique: Strongest feature: The reply supplies positive causal background rather than merely attacking naturalistic gaps, correctly noting that familiar minds can generate functional information and deliberately adjusted systems. Principal limitation: The analogy traverses substantial domain differences from human artifacts to biological and cosmic structures, and all observed designing minds are embodied, localized, temporally active, and dependent on physical energy. Live burden: The argument must identify genuinely shared causal features, avoid equivocal movement among information, fine-tuning, and specificity, and justify extrapolation from embodied agency to a transcendent designer with discriminating predictions. Locked score: The strong band reflects direct central relevance and meaningful evidential contact with demands for positive support, while preserving the locked findings of materially overstated uniqueness, unstable terminology, incomplete qualification, limited representational charity, and unresolved source-target disanalogies.

con-embodied-minds-analogy-limit.words: Every observed designing mind is embodied, localized, and energy-dependent, limiting extrapolation to an immaterial transcendent cosmic agent.
con-embodied-minds-analogy-limit.critique: Strongest feature: The reply pinpoints multiple causally relevant disanalogies between familiar designers and the proposed transcendent agent, directly limiting what experiential evidence about human minds can establish. Principal limitation: Observed embodiment does not prove that embodiment is essential to agency, so the argument constrains analogical support without demonstrating that an immaterial or nonlocalized mind is impossible. Live burden: The case must explain why bodily realization, spatial localization, and energy dependence are evidentially integral rather than contingent features, while permitting the opposing side to offer an independently warranted theory of disembodied agency. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptionally precise diagnostic contact, excellent central relevance, stable qualification, and strong representational charity, while preserving the modest calibration limit that an absence of observed transcendent designers establishes an extrapolation problem rather than a metaphysical impossibility.

con-divine-intentions-underdetermined.words: Design predicts fine-tuning only through defensible expectations about divine intentions, which suffering and theological uncertainty make difficult to specify.
con-divine-intentions-underdetermined.critique: Strongest feature: The reply exposes an important internal tension: design confirmation needs expectations about divine purposes, whereas skeptical uncertainty about those purposes weakens the very prediction that fine-tuning supposedly confirms. Principal limitation: The argument compresses the possibility that broad theistic commitments could modestly favor embodied moral agents without predicting a suffering-free, uniquely optimized, or otherwise narrowly specified universe. Live burden: The case must compare likelihoods under clearly articulated intention models, justify the relevance of suffering to cosmic habitability, and show that broad creator expectations remain too flexible to discriminate design from alternatives. Locked score: The very strong band reflects direct diagnostic force, stable scope, high central relevance, and substantial logical coherence, while preserving a measured evidential limitation because underdetermined intentions weaken confirmation without demonstrating that every proportionate theistic expectation is unavailable.

strengths: Built a cumulative beginning case from expansion, background radiation, galaxy ages, and major cosmological theorems while expressly stopping short of deductive proof.
Pressed quantum, bouncing, inflationary, and multiverse proposals on their retained laws, boundary conditions, information, fine-tuning, and combined theoretical commitments.
Presented fine-tuning as a concrete conjunction of life-sensitive constants and initial conditions rather than as a generic appeal to cosmic order.
Offered positive causal background for agency by connecting familiar minds with functional information and deliberately adjusted systems.

blunders.text: The beginning argument did not consistently distinguish a hot early phase, geodesic incompleteness, a classical boundary, and absolute origination.
The fine-tuning case moved from apparent contingency and narrow ranges toward improbability without establishing a defensible possibility space or probability measure.
The agency inference insufficiently answered the extrapolation from embodied human designers to a transcendent immaterial cause or supplied discriminating intentions and predictions.

strengths: Clearly separated empirical evidence for a hot dense early universe from evidence for a singularity or absolute beginning.
Explained why classical singularity theorems cannot determine the quantum-gravity regime and appropriately used that limitation to support uncertainty.
Identified the missing possibility space and probability measure beneath numerical fine-tuning claims.
Supplied a concrete anthropic prediction concerning the cosmological constant rather than defending the multiverse as a bare possibility.
Directly challenged both the embodiment analogy and the underdetermination of divine intentions required for design predictions.

blunders.text: The science-history reply sometimes answered a necessity claim stronger than Meyer's narrower contention that biblical ideas historically encouraged modern science.
The denial of empirical evidence for a singularity was phrased too categorically to acknowledge indirect, model-mediated evidential support.
The embodied-mind objection limits experiential support for transcendent agency but cannot establish that embodiment is metaphysically necessary for every possible mind.

newArguments.title: Robustness Without Exact Priors
newArguments.text: Fine-tuning need not depend on one canonical probability distribution. Investigators can test whether life-permitting conditions remain atypically constrained across multiple physically motivated parameterizations, dependency structures, and scale choices. If the apparent sensitivity disappears under many reasonable representations, the design case weakens; if it persists across them, the phenomenon acquires limited robustness despite unresolved exact priors. This approach converts the measure objection into a research program and supports only comparative evidential weight, not a numerical probability of design.

novelty.explanation: This is a new robustness-analysis framework not advanced by either participant and therefore has no transcript source move.

newArguments.title: Cross-Domain Constraint Signature
newArguments.text: The design analogy can be disciplined by identifying a narrow signature rather than equating every complex system with an artifact. The relevant features would be independently specified functional constraints, coordinated satisfaction of several constraints, and the absence of a demonstrated mechanism that makes those constraints probable. Evidence for agency would rise only when all features occur and would fall when natural processes reproduce them. This framework acknowledges embodiment differences and creates explicit conditions under which the analogical inference can be strengthened, weakened, or abandoned.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new falsifiable constraint-signature test for controlling the agency analogy across different causal domains.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that current cosmology warrants disciplined agnosticism because neither beginning evidence nor fine-tuning presently supplies likelihoods that distinguish transcendent design from empirically developing naturalistic models.

novelty.explanation: This integrates the participant's strongest objections into a unified comparative thesis without claiming naturalism has been proved.

premises.text: Observations establish a hot dense early phase, while conclusions about singularities, geodesic boundaries, or absolute beginnings depend on theoretical assumptions whose applicability fails or remains uncertain in quantum regimes.

novelty.explanation: This extends the transcript distinction by explicitly separating three different boundary conclusions and their theoretical dependencies.

premises.text: A scientifically serious alternative must earn credibility through mathematical coherence, independent motivation, retrodictive integration, or risky observational consequences rather than through logical possibility alone.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the model-plurality argument by supplying graded criteria for deciding which alternatives genuinely contribute to uncertainty.

premises.text: Fine-tuning cannot support a strong improbability inference until the relevant alternatives, dependencies, and measure are justified, although weaker sensitivity evidence may remain worthy of investigation.

novelty.explanation: This preserves the measure objection while avoiding the excessive conclusion that sensitivity evidence has no possible significance.

premises.text: Anthropic reasoning deserves credit proportional to its genuine predictive successes, but those successes must be reconstructed against preregistered assumptions and compared with rival likelihoods.

novelty.explanation: This strengthens the cited prediction while repairing the risk of treating one approximate success as confirmation of an entire framework.

premises.text: A transcendent designer remains weakly discriminating unless independent reasons specify its capacities and purposes, because familiar embodied agency does not by itself determine cosmic intentions or expected observations.

novelty.explanation: This combines the embodiment and intention objections into a single limitation on the design hypothesis's evidential likelihood.

conclusion.text: Therefore, continued naturalistic investigation and provisional agnosticism are presently better warranted than a design conclusion, while future evidence could revise that comparison in either direction.

novelty.explanation: This proportionate conclusion repairs any slide from current underdetermination to a categorical denial of possible design evidence.

newArguments.title: Predictive Compression Audit
newArguments.text: Competing explanations can be compared by how much observed structure they compress after counting adjustable assumptions. A useful audit would list each model's free parameters, selection rules, auxiliary mechanisms, independently supported components, and successful risky expectations. Design would receive no automatic penalty for being nonphysical, and naturalistic models would receive no automatic credit for mathematical vocabulary. The preferred account would be the one producing the greatest genuine predictive compression with the fewest unconstrained choices. Presently, divine intentions appear highly adjustable, so design supplies limited compression.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new symmetrical predictive-compression audit not stated by either participant and maps to no source move.

newArguments.title: Discovery Versus Accommodation Test
newArguments.text: The evidential force of both anthropic and design explanations depends on whether their expectations preceded the relevant observations. A structured historical test should record what parameter range was predicted, which assumptions were fixed beforehand, how broad the tolerance was, and whether failed alternatives were retained or discarded. The same standard should examine claims that theism expected a life-permitting universe. This procedure would distinguish risky discovery from flexible accommodation and prevent either side from receiving confirmation merely because its framework can be adjusted after observing the cosmos.

novelty.explanation: This is a new historical preregistration test for comparing anthropic and theistic expectations without asymmetrical evidential standards.
